id: typescript-etherpad-unescaped-export-attr-and-default-credentials
title: Unescaped data-* attribute in HTML export and no default/placeholder credential check in settings
summary: 'The HTML export builds a tag string such as `span data-NAME="VALUE"` from pad attribute pool
  content without escaping, so a quote or angle bracket in the value breaks out of the attribute and injects
  HTML or script into exported documents (stored XSS). The settings loader also validated the cookie prefix
  and went straight on to DB handling, without warning that accounts or SSO clients still use shipped
  placeholder passwords or secrets. Placeholder credentials left in place give attackers easy access.

  '
cwe:
- CWE-79
- CWE-1392
severity: high
confidence: medium
languages:
- typescript
source:
  kind: fix-commit
  ref: 86c56cf827dd6e5ff1b6cd3760f87adc47f58bb1
  vulnerable_ref: 86c56cf827dd6e5ff1b6cd3760f87adc47f58bb1^
  patched_ref: 86c56cf827dd6e5ff1b6cd3760f87adc47f58bb1
  repository: https://github.com/ether/etherpad
rule:
  message: 'Either an exported HTML tag interpolates a data-* attribute name/value without escaping (use
    Security.escapeHTMLAttribute and restrict the name to [a-zA-Z0-9_-]), or reloadSettings moves from
    cookie validation to DB handling without checking for default/placeholder user passwords or SSO client
    secrets.

    '
  pattern-either:
  - patterns:
    - pattern-either:
      - pattern: $TAGS.push(`span data-${$NAME[...]}="${$VAL[...]}"`)
      - pattern: $TAGS.push(`span data-${$NAME}="${$VAL}"`)
    - pattern-not: $TAGS.push(`span data-${$N}="${Security.escapeHTMLAttribute(...)}"`)
  - pattern: "if (<... $S.cookie.prefix ...>) {\n  ...\n}\nif ($S.dbType === 'dirty') {\n  ...\n}\n"
fix:
  guidance: Never interpolate pad-attribute-derived names or values directly into exported HTML. Strip
    the data-* attribute name down to alphanumerics, underscores and hyphens, and pass the value through
    Security.escapeHTMLAttribute (coerced with String). In settings loading, compare configured user passwords
    and SSO client secrets against a set of known placeholder values and log a loud warning (error level
    in production) before the instance is exposed.
  example: 'const dataName = String(prop[0]).replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '''');

    tags.push(`span data-${dataName}="${Security.escapeHTMLAttribute(String(prop[1]))}"`);


    const weakPasswords = new Set([''changeme1'', ''changeme'', ''admin'', ''password'', '''']);

    const offenders = Object.keys(users).filter((n) => weakPasswords.has(users[n].password));

    if (offenders.length) logger.warn(`Default password in use for: ${offenders.join('', '')}`);

    '
